target: inert subtree focus and interaction semantics
observed_behavior: The HTML Standard's inert-subtree model specifies hit-testing equivalent to pointer-events:none, text selection equivalent to user-select:none, non-editability for editable inert nodes, generally unavailable focus, and non-exposure to accessibility APIs; the user agent should omit inert nodes from find-in-page but may permit user overrides for finding or selection. A present boolean inert attribute makes an element and flat-tree descendants inert unless they escape this through the defined modal-dialog mechanism.
context: W07 B2 K3 read-only observation; WHATWG HTML Living Standard authoritative for the described native HTML mechanisms and guarded algorithms only; source shows Last Updated 20 July 2026.
limitations: The default is non-inert; not all offscreen, visually hidden or inactive-looking elements are thereby inert.
The explicit exception for top-layer modal dialog escape of ancestor inertness must be retained; the dialog can be inert through its own inert attribute.
The WHATWG text cautions against marking vital unobscured content inert, and notes that individual form controls usually have more appropriate disabled semantics.
Specification effects and user-agent allowances do not establish observed browser accessibility output, keyboard test PASS, or suitable app design.
